source.title: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning
source.authors: Gokul Gowri; Igor Sadalski; D. Raviv; P. Yin; Jonathan S. Rosenfeld; Allon M. Klein

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and supplemental text are present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures auxiliary mutual information against cell number and fits a saturating power law in biological representation models, a different metric and setting from the language-model loss scaling claim.
record.gate_note: The study's main noise-scaling experiments measure performance against measurement noise, not parameters, tokens, compute, or downstream task performance; those results do not test the listed versions. The cell-number scaling result is recorded because it tests power-law scaling in a non-language-model setting. Image and protein experiments vary noise, not model or dataset scale.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (single-cell transcriptomic representation models), it fits a saturating power law of auxiliary-MI performance against training cell number. That bears on V5 (power-law form beyond text pretraining). The measure is probe mutual information, not held-out loss, and the cell-number sweep is a baseline check, not the paper's focus. This is T3 rather than T2: it is a new domain, not a different method aimed at the original LM question.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find auxiliary-MI follows a saturating power law in cell number (as a baseline) and a distinct logarithmic law in measurement noise. They propose noise as an additional scaling axis and defer a joint law with model size and compute.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of language-model loss scaling: it measures auxiliary mutual information in cellular representation models, including cell-number and measurement-noise effects, rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy across parameters, tokens, or compute.

fits_no_version.finding: Performance vs measurement noise (SNR) follows a logarithmic/sigmoidal law derived from Gaussian channels. The authors say it is evidently not a power law. Theory curves fit 193 curves from 1,670 models with R² 0.979.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation performance scales predictably with measurement noise along a distinct, non-power-law axis.

record.problems: The scaling metric is auxiliary mutual information rather than held-out loss, and the cell-number scaling sample counts are inconsistent between the main text (80 models, 8 curves) and the Fig. 2 caption (120 models, 3 tasks and 4 metrics).
record.rows_left_out: Noise-versus-performance results for transcriptomic, image, and protein-sequence models were not included because they vary measurement noise rather than a resource axis in the listed claim versions. The paper also discusses model-family differences in saturation and noise robustness, which do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Scaling with parameters or compute in non-text settings: ESM2 comes in 8M/35M/150M sizes, but no size-scaling result is reported. No held-out-loss scaling. Image and protein experiments vary only noise, not data or model scale.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No downstream scaling with LM scale or loss.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents across setups.

missing.what: Per-model cell-number scaling parameters (I∞, Nsat, s): Nsat < 10^4 for most models, PCA saturates at tens of cells, random projection shows no scaling

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The cell-number scaling is a sanity check for the MI metric, not the main result. The noise-scaling results do not bear on any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token trends.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.

Tests cell-number scaling in cellular representation models using auxiliary mutual information, not held-out loss or scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute. The image and protein experiments vary measurement noise rather than model or dataset scale; other training regimes are not tested.
No downstream-task performance scaling or prediction from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations across fitting choices, and no test of departures from a single power law on the claim's resource axes.

rows.subject: Neural network-based representation models (aggregate; 80 models)
rows.operation_detail: Fit auxiliary mutual information as a function of the number of training cells N.
rows.measure: Auxiliary mutual information I(N), fitted with I(N) = I∞ − (N/Nsat)^−s; goodness of fit R².
rows.locator: Results, “Cell number scaling for cellular representations”; Fig. 2a–b
rows.note: The authors describe the result as a saturating power law across the neural-network models and auxiliary tasks. The text reports n = 80 models comprising 8 scaling curves; the Fig. 2 caption separately gives n = 120 models across 3 tasks and 4 metrics.
rows.check: State partial is defensible. The saturating power law fits the neural-network models (R² 0.90 ± 0.02), but S.III says most models have Nsat < 10^4 cells, below the actual dataset sizes, so the power-law regime is short and performance is largely saturated. Random projection shows no scaling behaviour and was omitted. Sample counts are inconsistent: the text gives n = 80 models and 8 curves, while the Fig. 2 caption gives n = 120 across 3 tasks and 4 metrics. The subject should say neural-network models (Geneformer, scVI), with PCA's parameters reported in Fig. S2.

relationships.condition: Neural-network single-cell representation models (Geneformer, scVI), auxiliary-MI vs training cell number
relationships.reason: A saturating power law I∞ − (N/Nsat)^−s fits with R² 0.90 ± 0.02 across models and tasks (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Auxiliary mutual information fitted I∞−(N/Nsat)^−s with R²=0.90±0.02 across models and tasks.

relationships.condition: Same models at dataset sizes above ~10^4 cells, and non-neural baselines
relationships.reason: Per S.III, most Nsat < 10^4 cells, so performance is largely saturated with respect to cell number, and random projection shows no scaling. The power-law regime spans a limited range, and the metric is probe MI, not loss (R1; text-based).
relationships.display_finding: Most saturation thresholds were below 10^4 cells, leaving probe mutual information largely saturated at larger sizes; random projection showed no scaling.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
